Running a mile on the first day? Experiencing pain? This concerns me. I want your workouts to be sustainable, man. Take things easy to begin with. It's more about building the habit at the beginning than actually losing weight. I know you're motivated and rearing to go, but I implore you to take it easy, especially at the beginning.

Have you heard of Couch to 5 Kilometres? It's a running program that builds up from the very basics. There are lots of free apps for it on Android and iOS. You may find it stupidly easy in the beginning since you're already running a mile, but it's good for things to be easy in the beginning. That's what makes any habit stick. It's more important to be consistent rather than to see results. The results will follow later.

Also, about the pain. Like someone said, better shoes could help. Your shoes influence your gait more than you realize. I had joint pains when I started, but getting running shoes with the thinnest soles I could find helped, because I was forced to work on getting my form right or else I'd easily hurt myself. Read more about this kind of thing here. You don't have to run barefeet, but the principle is useful to know.

Your new shoes don't have to be too expensive. I run in 40$ Kappa shoes that I found in a department store and I'm really pleased with them, so don't feel like you have to shell out. Just get the the fit right. Not too tight, not too loose. Once on, your shoe should stay on comfortably even without your laces tied. Run a few laps inside the store to get a feel for them. It's difficult to judge shoes in so small a time, but do the best that you can and don't sweat it.

I'm sorry to be giving you advice unasked for, but I just want your workouts to be sustainable and in the end for you to be the happiest you can be. :)

Exactly what it says on the tin: I propose that Voat should have the ability to post text with a link post. The text would be visible when you go to the comments section and could be used to give a photo credit or backstory, quote a small selection of a linked article (i.e. posting the relevant section in TIL), or a conversation starter. The layout of the comments page would match that of a text post, but with the title leading to the linked post.

For subs that have a rule that requires certain information to be submitted with links, it can be submitted directly to the post itself instead of as a comment. This ensures that vital information is visible to anyone that opens the comment sections without having to have OP make a comment that may or may not be buried or ignored.

Disclosure: I got this idea from Hubski, which allows what I am describing.
The ability to add text to a Link Post
